name: Modi's Narayan Pedhewale
why_it_matters: Satari Kandi Pedha is Satara district's geographically-protected dairy sweet — granular-textured khoa pedha (distinct from Mumbai/Mathura mawa pedha). Modi's Narayan Pedhewale in Mangalwar Peth is one of two original Modi family pedha shops in old Satara, alongside Ashok Modi at Powai Naka. The take-away box is the standard Satara souvenir.
insider_tip: Buy a 250g box (₹250) for the road — Kandi pedha stays fresh 5-7 days in cool weather. Cash + UPI; no cards at the counter. Open 9am-9pm.

name: Ashok Modi Satari Kandi Pedhewale
why_it_matters: Ashok Modi is the other historic Modi pedha shop in Satara — main outlet at Moti Chowk, additional retail at Powai Naka. Hygienic + fresh kandi pedha; the seasonal Amba Barfi (April-June, made with Hapus alphonso pulp from Konkan) is the under-the-radar specialty. Now has a Pune branch (Karve Nagar) for inter-city customers.
insider_tip: Amba barfi (₹400/250g) is only April-June — the alphonso-pulp seasonal pedha you can't get outside Satara. Buy at Moti Chowk's main outlet for the freshest batch. Cash + UPI.

name: Manas
why_it_matters: Top-rated sit-down in Satara on Tripadvisor with 135+ reviews — the mutton thali is the headline order, traditional Maharashtrian preparations including sukka mutton. The standard Kaas-plateau base lunch for travellers who want a non-thali sit-down. AC dining.
insider_tip: Mutton thali (₹450-550) at lunch is the order; Maharashtrian-style means leaner masala + more sol kadhi than the Kolhapuri tambda/pandhra rassa style. Open 11am-3:30pm + 7-10:30pm. Cards + UPI.

name: Gandharv Pure Veg
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor 4.5/5 — Satara's pure-veg sit-down specialising in rural Maharashtrian dishes. Patodi rassa (gram-flour log in spicy gravy) is the under-the-radar Satara-Sangli district signature most Maharashtra restaurants don't serve. The right post-Kaas-plateau drive lunch for non-meat travellers.
insider_tip: Patodi rassa (₹180) is the order — ask the waiter for the village-style preparation, not the watered-down restaurant version. Open 11am-3pm + 7-10pm. Cash + UPI.

name: Hotel Shreeman
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor 4.4/5 — described as 'best pure veg in Satara'. Table-service Maharashtrian + Indo-Chinese for groups with kids. Useful as a backup to Gandharv when their queue is full or the rural-specialty menu is too narrow.
insider_tip: Maharashtrian thali (₹300) at lunch is the order; the Indo-Chinese starters are the kid-friendly addition. Aamras seasonal April-June. Cards + UPI.
